open_points.subject: _confirmation_binding_digest and take_confirmation
open_points.text: _confirmation_binding_digest: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] MUST answer the hexadecimal text of a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous serialisation of the action, then the target, then the version, then every field of inputs in the order its model declares them, lists in the order given and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that equal arguments always give equal serialisations and so equal digests, and different arguments always different serialisations, two of which share a digest only by a collision of the digest itself, never by the serialisation; walking inputs it MUST take a model's fields, each name with its value in their declared order, and tell a model from any other value only through model_items, and take a tuple's elements in their order.
open_points.other_text:
A pending confirmation shown for one action, target, version and inputs
    is refused, and used up, when the submission carrying its value changes
    any one of them: another action, another target, another version or
    none, another value of any input, or the same list in another order
    (rule 6).
open_points.question: Must digest collisions be excluded from admissible histories, or must the retained binding distinguish colliding serialisations so that every changed input is refused?
